notes:
This is an early build, released to consoles set to Latest Updates.

Moonlight motion: Moonlight can now send gyro and tilt to the PC you stream from, for games that use motion. Handheld it uses the console's own motion sensor; with a Pro Controller or detached Joy-Cons it uses the controller's. The PC has to run Sunshine for motion to go through.

DraStic touch in portrait: with Handheld orientation set to Portrait, DraStic took touches only near the middle of the screen, and they landed in the wrong place. Taps now land where you touch, in portrait as in landscape.

Vertical arcade games: arcade games now have the Handheld orientation setting (Performance settings, General). Portrait turns the screen for vertical shooters, handheld only, and goes back when you quit. A grip that holds the controllers upright works best, since attached Joy-Cons keep their usual directions.

PlayStation Remote Play: a new tile in Ports and Apps (add it from Add ports and apps) streams your PS4 or PS5 with chiaki-ng. Its first start downloads it, then you link your console with its PIN; the on-screen keyboards in the pause menu type the PIN and the PSN sign-in. Video is decoded in software here, so 720p is the setting to pick.

PC game mods: each PC game on the web page has a DLL overrides button, for mods that ship their own DLL (a controller fix's dinput8, a graphics mod's d3d9). Type the DLL names and the game loads the mod's copy from its folder from the next launch.

Community settings: a game's first launch, and Apply recommended settings, no longer switch a game to AetherSX2, melonDS or RetroArch's PSP emulator, and no longer take settings measured on them. Many PS2 games went to AetherSX2 on their first launch this way. A recommendation also keeps the emulator you chose for that console instead of putting the game back on the default one. Games already switched keep the emulator they have; change it in the game's Performance settings.

New and lightly tested: Moonlight motion was not tried in a real stream, PlayStation Remote Play was not linked to a real console, and no vertical arcade game was tried in portrait.

stable.notes:
The 2.41 changes, now on the Stable channel. If this console was on 2.40.0,
it also gets the whole 2.40 series, summed up at the end.

This update carries a new boot script: the console restarts once for the
update and once more on its own about a minute after the first boot. Do not
power off while it says part 2 of 2.

The SD card's fastest mode (DDR200) is now used on Samsung cards only, as
Switchroot does. Other cards run in the standard mode: if yours used the
fast mode, games load a little slower, but SanDisk cards, which cannot run
it reliably on the Switch, no longer get read errors under load. If a
Samsung card gives read errors, turn DDR200 off in the SCCM Retro app's Boot
settings.

The SCCM Retro app on the Homebrew menu is now one app: Launch SCCM Retro,
Launch in Safe Mode (stock clocks and voltages, once), Options (WiFi and
Bluetooth, boot settings, auto launch), and installing or removing SCCM
Retro on an SD card. The separate installer and calibration apps are
removed.

Swap A and B now applies only to Gen1Recomp and Moonlight, the two games
that offer it.

New background: Arcade, in Settings, Display and Sound, Appearance.

From 2.40.0, also: the console boots in about 28 seconds instead of about
50; Ocarina of Time and Majora's Mask, and Mario Kart Wii as a native port
with Retro Rewind online, on Ports and Apps; a PC Games tab for Windows
games; auto save for RetroArch, 3DS and PS2 games; Wii U, GameCube, WiFi
and volume button fixes; and a security fix to install permissions.
